# SIcon `<s-icon>`

Displays an icon from the Polaris icon set by name. `SIcon` is the typed Vue 3 wrapper for Shopify's Polaris `<s-icon>` web component.

```ts
import { SIcon } from 'polaris-vue-elements'
```

## Best practices

- **Use icons to inform, not decorate.** An icon should explain what an action does or show a state, like a delete icon on a delete action or a check for something completed. Don't add icons just for looks.
- **Be consistent.** Once an icon stands for an action or concept, keep it that way across your whole app. If `edit` means editing in one place, use it for editing in every place.
- **Pair icons with text when you can.** On their own, even familiar icons can be read in more than one way. Use an icon alone only where space is tight, such as an icon-only button with an `accessibilityLabel`.
- **Pick widely recognized icons.** Favor icons with settled meanings, like `search`, `delete` and `plus`. If an icon needs explaining, choose a different one.
- **Let `tone` carry meaning.** Use `tone="critical"` for destructive actions, `tone="success"` for positive states and `tone="warning"` for caution. Tones should communicate something, not decorate.

```vue
<SIcon type="alert-triangle" tone="warning" />
```

See [Shopify's best practices for `<s-icon>`](https://shopify.dev/docs/api/app-home/latest/web-components/media-and-visuals/icon#best-practices) for the full guidance.

```vue
<script setup>

</script>

<template>
  <!-- `type` accepts a large named-icon union; a few examples below. See
       src/lib/generated/types.ts for the full list. -->
  <SIcon type="star" />
  <SIcon type="cart" tone="info" />
  <SIcon type="check-circle" tone="success" />
  <SIcon type="alert-triangle" tone="warning" />
  <SIcon type="delete" tone="critical" />
  <SIcon type="settings" size="small" color="subdued" />
</template>
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `color` | `"subdued" \| "base"` | The color emphasis level that controls visual intensity. - `base`: Primary color for body text, standard UI elements, and general content with good readability. - `subdued`: Deemphasized color for secondary text, supporting labels, and less critical interface elements. |
| `interestFor` | `string` | ID of a component that should respond to interest (e.g. hover and focus) on this component. |
| `size` | `"base" \| "small"` | The size of the icon. - `small`: Smaller icon suitable for inline use within text or compact UI elements. - `base`: Default size that works well for standalone icons and standard use cases. |
| `tone` | `"auto" \| "neutral" \| "info" \| "success" \| "caution" \| "warning" \| "critical"` | The semantic meaning and color treatment of the component. - `info`: Informational content or helpful tips. - `success`: Positive outcomes or successful states. - `warning`: Important warnings about potential issues. - `critical`: Urgent problems or destructive actions. - `auto`: Automatically determined based on context. - `neutral`: General information without specific intent. - `caution`: Advisory notices that need attention. |
| `type` | `"color" \| "info" \| "adjust" \| "affiliate" \| "airplane" \| "alert-bubble" \| "alert-circle" \| "alert-diamond" … (553 more)` | The icon to display from the icon library. Set to a valid icon name to display that icon. To hide the icon completely, use an empty string `''`. To reserve the icon's space without displaying an icon, use `'empty'`. |

> Some type columns above are truncated for readability; the full union is available in the library's generated TypeScript types (`src/lib/generated/types.ts`).
